items.title: Joseph "Red" Clark Interview, 1959-11-11
items.q: He said, that's just what I want. He says, I want somebody like you that I can train to myself. I said, all right.

ctx.x: First job of any kind. Of any kind?

Well I'll tell you, they set this concert band up, this fellow Pritchett. He set this band up. Well I had been practicing a lot and I'd been pinch hitting around with little bands all around, you know, different bands and all. So Willie Wilson, he was leading the record band at that time. And I knew Willie when he first came here. I knew him when he first came. He and Johnny. Willie worked at Sherwood's Pharmacy, which used to be at Canal and Durgin Wall. And Johnny, his brother, which was the baritone player, he…

items.title: Joseph "Red" Clark Interview, 1959-01-13
items.q: Because I was playing in a concert band at that time. It says a man here by the name of Henry Pritchett. He set up a concert band of thirty pieces.

ctx.x: You weren't one of the founders then?

No I'm not a founder. But it hadn't been organized very long when I joined. But I remember when it was organized. Because I was playing in a concert band at that time. It says a man here by the name of Henry Pritchett. He set up a concert band of thirty pieces. Still here? Oh he's still here. Yes. But I mean he don't fool with any bands anymore because he's pretty foreign age now.
You still live down there near St. Bernard someplace?
